extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, historians and philosophers of mathematics, advanced students interested in the nature of mathematical practice
extracted.subtask_description: An essayistic/historical account articulating standards and characteristic features by which mathematical activity can be understood and (implicitly) evaluated — e.g., relation to empirical science, axiomatization, rigour, style, and philosophical foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to the natural sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The most vitally characteristic fact about mathematics is, in my opinion, its quite peculiar relationship to the natural sciences, or, more generally, to any science which interprets experience on a higher than purely descriptive level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematics is closely linked with the natural sciences: some of the best inspirations originate in the natural sciences; mathematical methods pervade and dominate theoretical divisions of the natural sciences. This relationship is a central criterion for understanding mathematical development and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to mathematical method as criterion of scientific success
rubrics_metrics.description: In modern empirical sciences it has become more and more a major criterion of success whether they have become accessible to the mathematical method or to the near-mathematical methods of physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a scientific discipline admits mathematical formulation and methods is used as a measure of its progress; this shapes what mathematicians and scientists value in theoretical development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicity of mathematics (empirical vs. abstract)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a quite peculiar duplicity in the nature of mathematics. One has to realize this duplicity, to accept it, and to assimilate it into one's thinking on the subject. This double face is the face of mathematics...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematics simultaneously displays empirical origins/applications and highly abstract, de-empirized branches. Evaluations of mathematical work should accept and accommodate both aspects rather than force a single unified characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiomatization/postulational treatment as a methodological move
rubrics_metrics.description: Euclid's postulational treatment represents a great step away from empiricism, but it is not at all simple to defend the position that this was the decisive and final step, producing an absolute separation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A postulational/axiomatic presentation is an important methodological standard, but axiomatization does not by itself render mathematics wholly independent of empirical considerations; historical examples show postulates often rest on physical insight and experimental verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical/physical evidence can determine mathematical frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea that in at least one significant sense—and in spite of all mathematico-logical analyses—the decision for or against Euclid may have to be empirical, was certainly present... The discovery of general relativity forced a revision of our views on the relationship of geometry...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice among competing mathematical frameworks (e.g., Euclidean vs. non-Euclidean geometry) may ultimately be guided by empirical/physical discoveries; empirical confirmation can have the final say in adopting mathematical structures for modeling reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical origins and inspiration (geometry and calculus examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the best inspirations in mathematics... have come from the natural sciences. The first example is geometry. The second example is calculus — or rather all of analysis, which sprang from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many central mathematical developments originated from empirical problems (surveying/geometry, mechanics leading to calculus). Recognizing empirical origin is part of assessing the character and purpose of mathematical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical advance/exact thinking as hallmark
rubrics_metrics.description: The calculus was the first achievement of modern mathematics, and it is difficult to overestimate its importance... the system of mathematical analysis ... still constitutes the greatest technical advance in exact thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The degree to which a contribution advances exact technical methods and sharpness of thought is a key positive criterion for valuing mathematical work, even when earlier formulations were not fully rigorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variability of the concept of mathematical rigour
rubrics_metrics.description: The variability of the concept of rigour shows that something else besides mathematical abstraction must enter into the makeup of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigour is historically contingent and changes with intellectual context; what counts as rigorous in one era may be insufficient in another. Evaluators should be sensitive to historical standards and the evolving notion of rigour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style of proofs and presentation matters
rubrics_metrics.description: It is well known that the style in which mathematical proofs are written has undergone considerable fluctuations... In fields in which differences are present, they are mainly differences in presentation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation and stylistic choices can affect perceived rigour and clarity. Some differences are superficial and removable, while others are essential and may require new theories to resolve; assessors should distinguish presentation-variance from substantive methodological differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for semi-physical or non-rigorous methods when productive
rubrics_metrics.description: The first formulations of the calculus were not even mathematically rigorous. An inexact, semi-physical formulation was the only one available for over a hundred and fifty years after Newton!... Some of the leading mathematical spirits of the period were clearly not rigorous... Yet no mathematician would want to exclude it from the fold - that period produced mathematics as first class as ever existed!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effectiveness and the ability to yield deep results can justify temporarily non-rigorous or semi-physical methods; historical precedent shows major advances emerged before later rigorous foundations were developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical/epistemological components influence mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Something nonmathematical, somehow connected with the empirical sciences or with philosophy or both, does enter essentially—and its non-empirical character could only be maintained if one assumed that philosophy (or more specifically epistemology) can exist independently of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical foundations and acceptability are influenced by broader philosophical or epistemological positions; debates about foundations reveal that non-mathematical considerations (philosophy, epistemology, relation to experience) matter for judging mathematical work.
